The other classes there are errors, helpers or matchers (UnsafeSqlError, RlsError, SecretColumnMatcher, _CatalogView, _Scoping, _BodyTextCache and similar), and none subclass SqlRunner. A tree-wide grep for SqlRunner subclasses found only SqliteRunner and MySQLRunner besides these, and both are outside safety/. RefusalRedactingRunner (rule_sets.py:983-1016) catches UnsafeSqlError and RlsError, so it covers every refusal type (RuleSetRefusal, WholeRowSelectError, RlsError), and it logs at WARNING. But the claim says it logs the full reason, and that fails for one path. When a refusal has a non-refusal __cause__, _logged_by_guard (971-980) assumes the guard already logged the cause, and line 1011 then logs only the kind fields (the exception text is dropped). rls.py:265-273 raises RlsError('could not analyze SQL scopes ...: {e}') from e when traverse_scope fails, and rls.py has no logger at all (grep 'logg' finds no match). That RlsError therefore reaches the redactor with a non-refusal cause, gets redacted to REDACTED_RLS, and its full reason is logged nowhere. The docstring at 984 and the glossary claim 'log the full reason at WARNING' for every refusal, so this case contradicts them. Also, RuleSetRefusal is re-raised unchanged (1002-1004) and its reason is logged by RuleSetGuardRunner (880), which is fine. Guard-internal errors get REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR (961), which is not a refusal kind.

policy.py:38-40 unauthenticated_non_loopback returns cfg.auth.mode == 'none' and not is_loopback_host(cfg.server.host); policy.py:13-18 holds the refusal message naming the SQLLENS_AUTH__INSECURE override. The escape is applied by the policy's callers: transport/http.py:229-231 raises ValueError when the predicate holds and not cfg.auth.insecure; cli.py:227-233 and 283-289 exit 2 under the same condition, and with insecure true they only warn. So the rule as a whole (predicate and message from policy.py, escape at the call sites) refuses mode none on a non-loopback host unless auth.insecure. Caveat: policy.py itself does not read auth.insecure (its docstring says the predicate is independent of opt-out), so the glossary's attribution of the whole rule to that file is loose but the behavior is accurate. is_loopback_host treats localhost, loopback IPs and IPv4-mapped loopback as loopback, and fails closed on wildcards and other hostnames.

check_catalog (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:1118-1190) does check that every listed table (BASE TABLE) and column exists, and it runs at startup via preflight.probe_database -> _check_rule_set_catalog (preflight.py:151-154, 166) when a rule-set file is configured on MySQL. But the type check is narrower than the glossary claims: only `typed` entries from _catalog_reads (rules_sets.py:1091-1100) are compared against DATA_TYPE (lines 1178-1186). Those are compare-rule columns, parent_rule compare columns, and owner_via link_user_column. Ordinary listed columns, predicate columns and link row/target columns are checked for existence only, with no type check. The glossary line (docs/internal/glossary.md:11) says every table and column exists 'with the expected type', which overstates this. The check_catalog docstring itself limits type checking to compare columns and link_user_column. The check also runs at request time via ensure_catalog_confirmed, not only at startup, which the glossary does not say.
